text: If $I(x)=\int e^{\sin ^{2}x}(\cos x\sin 2x-\sin x)dx$ and $I(0)=1$, then $I\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{Given,}I(x)=\int e^{\sin ^{2}x}(\cos x\sin 2x-\sin x)dx \\  \\ =\int e^{\sin ^{2}x}\cdot \cos x\cdot \sin 2xdx-\int \sin xe^{\sin ^{2}x}dx \\  \\ =\int \dfrac{\cos x}{\mathrm{I}}\cdot \dfrac{e^{\sin ^{2}x}\cdot \sin 2x}{\mathrm{II}}dx-\int \sin x\cdot e^{\sin ^{2}x}dx \\  \\ =\cos x\cdot e^{\sin ^{2}x}-\int (-\sin x)e^{\sin ^{2}x}dx-\int \sin xe^{\sin ^{2}x}dx \\  \\ =\cos x\cdot e^{\sin ^{2}x}+\int \sin xe^{\sin ^{2}x}\cdot dx-\int \sin x\cdot e^{\sin ^{2}x}dx+C \end{array}$

$I(x)=e^{\sin ^{2}x}\cdot \cos x+C$

Given, $I(0)=1\Rightarrow C=0$

So, $I(x)=e^{\sin ^{2}x}\cdot \cos x$

$\Rightarrow I(π/3)=e^{3/4}\cdot \frac{1}{2}=\frac{e^{3/4}}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: The shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x+2}{1}=\frac{y}{-2}=\frac{z-5}{2}$ and $\frac{x-4}{1}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z+3}{0}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, the lines are

$\begin{array}{ll} \dfrac{x+2}{1} & =\dfrac{y}{-2}=\dfrac{z-5}{2}..........(i) \\  \\ \text{and}\dfrac{x-4}{1} & =\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z+3}{0}..........(ii) \end{array}$

Formula for shortest distance between two skew-lines,

$\begin{array}{llllllllllllllllllllllllll} SD & =\left |\dfrac{\right |\begin{array}{lll} x_{2}-x_{1} & y_{2}-y_{1} & z_{2}-z_{1} \\ a_{1} & b_{1} & c_{1} \\ a_{2} & b_{2} & c_{2} \end{array}\left |}{\right |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{𝐢} & \hat{𝐣} & \hat{𝐤} \\ a_{1} & b_{1} & c_{1} \\ a_{2} & b_{2} & c_{2} \end{array}\left |}\right |=\left |\dfrac{\right |\begin{array}{lll} 6 & 1 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \end{array}\left |}{\right |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{𝐢} & \hat{𝐣} & \hat{𝐤} \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \end{array}\left |}\right | \\  \\ =\left |\dfrac{6(-4)-1(-2)-8(4)}{|-4\hat{𝐢}+2\hat{𝐣}+4\hat{𝐤}|}\right | \\  \\ =\left |\dfrac{-24+2-32}{\sqrt{36}}\right | \\  \\ =\left |\dfrac{-54}{6}\right |=|-9|=9 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: Let the ellipse $E:x^{2}+9y^{2}=9$ intersect the positive x and y-axes at the points A and B respectively. Let the major axis of E be a diameter of the circle C. Let the line passing through A and B meet the circle C at the point P. If the area of the triangle with vertices A, P and the origin O is $\frac{m}{n}$, where m and n are coprime, then $m-n$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given equation of the ellipse is

$\begin{array}{l} x^{2}+9y^{2}=9..........(i) \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{x^{2}}{9}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{1}=1 \end{array}$

Now, equation of line $AB$ is

$x+3y=3$...........(ii)


[IMG]


Now, point of intersection of line $x+3y=3$ and circle

$\begin{array}{ll}  & x^{2}+y^{2}=9 \\  \\  & \therefore (3-3y)^{2}+y^{2}=9 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow 9-18y+9y^{2}+y^{2}=9 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow -18y+10y^{2}=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow 18y=10y^{2} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow y=0,\frac{9}{5} \end{array}$

Now, from figure, we clearly see that vertices $A,P$ and $O$ makes a $△APO$, 

whose area is $\frac{1}{2}\times$ Base $\times$ Height

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Area}=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 3\times \dfrac{9}{5}=\dfrac{27}{10}=\dfrac{m}{n}[Given] \\  \\ \therefore m=27,n=10 \\  \\ \Rightarrow m-n=27-10=17 \end{array}$

text: Let O be the origin and the position vector of the point P be $-\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\widehat{k}$. If the position vectors of the points A, B and C are $-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\widehat{k},2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\widehat{k}$ and $-4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$ respectively, then the projection of the vector $OP\leftarrow$ on a vector perpendicular to the vectors $AB\leftarrow$ and $AC\leftarrow$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, the position vector of point P is :
$OP\leftarrow =-\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\widehat{k}$

Position vectors of points A, B, and C are :

$OA\leftarrow =-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\widehat{k}$

$OB\leftarrow =2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\widehat{k}$

$OC\leftarrow =-4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$

Now, vectors $AB\leftarrow$ and $AC\leftarrow$ can be calculated as :

$AB\leftarrow =OB\leftarrow -OA\leftarrow$

$=(2+2)\hat{i}+(4-1)\hat{j}+(-2+3)\widehat{k}$

$=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$

$AC\leftarrow =OC\leftarrow -OA\leftarrow$

$=(-4+2)\hat{i}+(2-1)\hat{j}+(-1+3)\widehat{k}$

$=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$

$\begin{array}{llllllll} \text{Now,}AB\leftarrow \times AC\leftarrow  & =\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{𝐢} & \hat{𝐣} & \hat{𝐤} \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 \end{array}\right | \\  \\ =\hat{𝐢}(5)+\hat{𝐣}(-2-8)+\hat{𝐤}(4+6) \\  \\ =5\hat{𝐢}-10\hat{𝐣}+10\hat{𝐤} \\  \\ OP\leftarrow =-\hat{𝐢}-2\hat{𝐣}+3\hat{𝐤} \end{array}$

To find the projection of $OP\leftarrow$ onto $AB\leftarrow \times AC\leftarrow$, we need to find the dot product between $OP\leftarrow$ and the normalized vector $AB\leftarrow \times AC\leftarrow$.

First, find the magnitude of $AB\leftarrow \times AC\leftarrow$ :

$|AB\leftarrow \times AC\leftarrow |=\sqrt{5^{2}+(-10)^{2}+10^{2}}$

$=\sqrt{25+100+100}$

$=\sqrt{225}$

$=15$

The projection of vector $OP\leftarrow$ onto a vector perpendicular to both $AB\leftarrow$ and $AC\leftarrow$ (which is $AB\leftarrow \times AC\leftarrow$) is given by :

$\frac{OP\leftarrow \cdot (AB\leftarrow \times AC\leftarrow )}{|AB\leftarrow \times AC\leftarrow |}$

= $\frac{(-\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\cdot (5\hat{i}-10\hat{j}+10\hat{k})}{\sqrt{25+100+100}}$

$=\frac{-5+20+30}{15}$

$=\frac{45}{15}=3$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: If $f(x)=\frac{(\tan 1^{\circ })x+\log _{e}(123)}{x\log _{e}(1234)-(\tan 1^{\circ })},x>0$, then the least value of $f(f(x))+f\left (f\left (\frac{4}{x}\right )\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that $f(x)=\frac{(\tan 1^{\circ })x+\log _{e}(123)}{x\log _{e}(1234)-(\tan 1^{\circ })}$

Let us consider a similar function of $(x)$, 

$\therefore f(x)=\frac{Ax+B}{Cx-A}$

$\text{Now,}$

$\begin{array}{l} f(f(x))=\dfrac{A\left (\frac{Ax+B}{Cx-A}\right )+B}{C\left (\frac{Ax+B}{Cx-A}\right )-A} \\  \\ =\dfrac{A^{2}x+AB+BCx-AB}{ACx+BC-ACx+A^{2}} \\  \\ =\dfrac{x\left (A^{2}+BC\right )}{(BC+A^{2})}=x \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \quad f(f(x))=x \\  \\ \text{Similarly,}f\left (f\left (\dfrac{4}{x}\right )\right )=\dfrac{4}{x} \\  \\ \text{Apply, AM}\geq \text{GM} \\  \\ \left (x+\dfrac{4}{x}\right )\geq 2\sqrt{x\cdot \dfrac{4}{x}}=4(x>0) \\  \\ \Rightarrow f(f(x))+f\left (f\left (\dfrac{4}{x}\right )\right )\geq 4 \end{array}$

Hence, the least value is 4 .
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: If the coefficient of $x^{7}$ in $\left (ax-\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{13}$ and the coefficient of $x^{-5}$ in $\left (ax+\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{13}$ are equal, then $a^{4}b^{4}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given expression is $\left (ax-\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{13}$

So,

$\begin{array}{ll} T_{r+1} & ={}^{13}C_{r}(ax)^{13-r}\left (-\dfrac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{r} \\  \\ ={}^{13}C_{r}(a)^{13-r}x^{13-r-2r}(-1/b)^{r} \\  \\ ={}^{13}C_{r}(a)^{13-r}\left (-\dfrac{1}{b}\right )^{r}x^{13-3r} \end{array}$

For coefficient of $x^{7}$ in $\left (ax-\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{13}$

$\begin{array}{l} 13-3r=7 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 3r=6\Rightarrow r=2 \\  \\ \therefore \text{Coefficient of}x^{7}={}^{13}C_{2}\cdot (a)^{11}\cdot \dfrac{1}{b^{2}} \end{array}$

Again, the another expression is $\left (ax+\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{13}$

So, $T_{r+1}={}^{13}C_{r}(ax)^{13-r}\left (\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{r}={}^{13}C_{r}(a)^{13-r}\left (\frac{1}{b}\right )^{r}x^{13-3r}$

For coefficient of $x^{-5}$ in $\left (ax+\frac{1}{bx^{2}}\right )^{13}$

$\begin{array}{l} 13-3r=-5 \\  \\ \Rightarrow r=6 \end{array}$

So, coefficient of $x^{-5}={}^{13}C_{6}(a)^{7}\frac{1}{b^{6}}$

Now, according to the question, 

${}^{13}C_{2}(a)^{11}\frac{1}{b^{2}}={}^{13}C_{6}(a)^{7}\frac{1}{b^{6}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow a^{4}b^{4}=\dfrac{{}^{13}C_{6}}{{}^{13}C_{2}} \\  \\ \therefore a^{4}b^{4}=22 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: An arc PQ of a circle subtends a right angle at its centre O. The mid point of the arc PQ is R. If $OP\leftarrow =\vec{u},OR\leftarrow =\vec{v}$, and $OQ\leftarrow =α\vec{u}+β\vec{v}$, then $α,β^{2}$ are the roots of the equation :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An arc $PQ$ of a circle subtends a right angle at its centre $O$. The mid-point of an $\mathrm{arc}PQ$ is $R$. So, $PR=RQ$ 

Also given that, $OP\leftarrow =\vec{u},OR\leftarrow =\vec{v}$, and $OQ\leftarrow =α\vec{u}+β\vec{v}$


[IMG]


Let $OP\leftarrow =\vec{u}$

$\begin{array}{l} OQ\leftarrow =\vec{q}=α\vec{u}+β\vec{v} \\  \\ OR\leftarrow =\vec{v} \end{array}$

Clearly, $\vec{q}=\hat{𝐣}$

$\vec{u}=\hat{𝐢},\vec{v}=\frac{\hat{𝐢}+\hat{𝐣}}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now, given, $\vec{q}=α\vec{u}+β\vec{v}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow  & \hat{𝐣}=α(\hat{𝐢})+β\left (\frac{\hat{𝐢}+\hat{𝐣}}{\sqrt{2}}\right ) \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & \hat{𝐣}=\hat{𝐢}\left (α+\frac{β}{\sqrt{2}}\right )+\frac{β}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{𝐣} \end{array}$

On comparing both sides, we get

$\begin{array}{l} α+\frac{β}{\sqrt{2}}=0\text{and}\frac{β}{\sqrt{2}}=1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow α=-\frac{β}{\sqrt{2}}\therefore β=\sqrt{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow α=-1,β^{2}=2 \end{array}$

Now, $α$ and $β^{2}$ are roots of the quadratic equation is $x^{2}-x-2=0$

text: Let N denote the sum of the numbers obtained when two dice are rolled. If the probability that $2^{N}<N!$ is $\frac{m}{n}$, where m and n are coprime, then $4m-3n$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$N$ denote the sum of the numbers obtained when two dice are rolled.

Such that $2^{N}<N$!

$\text{i.e.,}4\leq N\leq 12\text{i.e.,}N\in \{4,5,6,\ldots 12\}$

Now, $P(N=2)+P(N=3)=\frac{1}{36}+\frac{2}{36}=\frac{3}{36}=\frac{1}{12}$

So, required probability $=1-\frac{1}{12}=\frac{11}{12}=\frac{m}{n}$

$4m-3n=4\times 11-3\times 12=44-36=8$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: A square piece of tin of side 30 cm is to be made into a box without top by cutting a square from each corner and folding up the flaps to form a box. If the volume of the box is maximum, then its surface area (in cm${}^{2}$) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let a square of side $x$ cm be cut from each corner, $0<x<15$. The box has a square base of side $(30-2x)$ cm and height $x$ cm.


[IMG]

$V=x(30-2x)^{2}$

$\dfrac{dV}{dx}=(30-2x)^{2}-4x(30-2x)=(30-2x)(30-6x)$

In $0<x<15$, $\dfrac{dV}{dx}=0$ only at $x=5$; $\dfrac{dV}{dx}>0$ for $0<x<5$ and $\dfrac{dV}{dx}<0$ for $5<x<15$, so $V$ is maximum at $x=5$.

The box has no top, so its surface area is the base, a square of side $(30-2x)$, plus four side faces, each a rectangle of sides $(30-2x)$ and $x$:

$S=(30-2x)^{2}+4x(30-2x)$

At $x=5$: $S=20^{2}+4\times 5\times 20=400+400=800\text{cm}^{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: $96\cos \frac{π}{33}\cos \frac{2π}{33}\cos \frac{4π}{33}\cos \frac{8π}{33}\cos \frac{16π}{33}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let

$\begin{array}{l} A=96\cos \dfrac{π}{33}\cos \dfrac{2π}{33}\cos \dfrac{4π}{33}\cos \dfrac{8π}{33}\cos \dfrac{16π}{33} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2A=96\times 2\left (\cos \dfrac{π}{33}\cos \dfrac{2π}{33}\cos \dfrac{4π}{33}\cos \dfrac{8π}{33}\cos \dfrac{16π}{33}\right ) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2A\times \sin \dfrac{π}{33}=96\times \left (2\sin \dfrac{π}{33}\cos \dfrac{π}{33}\cos \dfrac{2π}{33}\cos \dfrac{4π}{33}\cdot \cos \dfrac{8π}{33}\cos \dfrac{16π}{33}\right ) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2A\times \sin \dfrac{π}{33}=6\times \sin \dfrac{32π}{33}=6\times \sin \dfrac{π}{33} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2A=6\Rightarrow A=3 \end{array}$

Thus, the required answer is 3 .

text:
For the system of linear equations

$2x-y+3z=5$

$3x+2y-z=7$

$4x+5y+αz=β$,

which of the following is NOT correct?
options: The system has infinitely many solutions for $α=-6$ and $β=9$
The system has a unique solution for $α$ $\neq$ $-5$ and $β=8$
The system is inconsistent for $α=-5$ and $β=8$
The system has infinitely many solutions for $α=-5$ and $β=9$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given system of linear equation is

$\begin{array}{lllllll} 2x-y+3z=5 \\  \\ 3x+2y-z=7 \\  \\ 4x+5y+αz=β \\  \\ \text{Now,}\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 5 & α \end{array}\right |=7(α+5) \end{array}$

So, this system of equation has unique solution, if $α\neq -5$

and $\Delta _{1}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 5 & -1 & 3 \\ 7 & 2 & -1 \\ β & 5 & α \end{array}\right |=17α-5β+130$

and $\Delta _{2}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 5 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 \\ 4 & β & α \end{array}\right |=11β-α-104$

and $\Delta _{3}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & -1 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & 7 \\ 4 & 5 & β \end{array}\right |=7(β-9)$

For infinitely many solutions,

$\Delta =\Delta _{1}=\Delta _{2}=\Delta _{3}=0$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{So,}\Delta =0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 7(α+5)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow α=-5 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta _{3}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 7(β-9)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow β=9 \end{array}$

If $α=-5$ and $β=8$, then $\Delta$ equals zero but $\Delta _{3}$ does not, which would imply the system is inconsistent for $α=-5$ and $β=8$.

Check the options: for $α=-6$ ($\neq -5$) the system has a unique solution, so option A (infinitely many solutions for $α=-6$, $β=9$) is NOT correct. Options B, C and D are correct statements (for $α=-5$, $β=9$ all of $\Delta ,\Delta _{1},\Delta _{2},\Delta _{3}$ vanish).

Therefore, the option that is NOT correct is A.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: A line segment AB of length $λ$ moves such that the points A and B remain on the periphery of a circle of radius $λ$. Then the locus of the point, that divides the line segment AB in the ratio 2 : 3, is a circle of radius :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Take the centre $O$ of the given circle as origin (the radius of the locus does not depend on the choice of axes). Let $C$ be the midpoint of $AB$ and $M(x,y)$ the point dividing $AB$ in the ratio $2:3$.

$OA=λ$, $AC=\dfrac{λ}{2}$ and $OC⟂AB$, so

$OC^{2}=λ^{2}-\frac{λ^{2}}{4}=\frac{3λ^{2}}{4}.$

$AM=\dfrac{2λ}{5}$, so $CM=AC-AM=\dfrac{λ}{2}-\dfrac{2λ}{5}=\dfrac{λ}{10}$.

In $△OCM$, right-angled at $C$,

$x^{2}+y^{2}=OM^{2}=OC^{2}+CM^{2}=\frac{3λ^{2}}{4}+\frac{λ^{2}}{100}=\frac{76λ^{2}}{100}=\frac{19λ^{2}}{25}.$

So $M$ moves on a circle concentric with the given one, of radius $\dfrac{\sqrt{19}}{5}λ$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: Let $f$ be a differentiable function such that $x^{2}f(x)-x=4\int\limits _{0}^{x}tf(t)dt$, $f(1)=\frac{2}{3}$. Then $18f(3)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that

$x^{2}f(x)-x=4\int\limits _{0}^{x}tf(t)dt$

On differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get

$\begin{array}{ll}  & 2xf(x)+x^{2}f^{'}(x)-1=4xf(x) \\  \\  & \Rightarrow x^{2}f^{'}(x)-2xf(x)-1=0 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow x^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}-2xy=1[\text{Let}y=f(x)] \\  \\  & \frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{2}{x}y=\frac{1}{x^{2}} \end{array}$

On comparing above equation with 

$\frac{dy}{dx}+Py=Q$, where $P=-\frac{2}{x},Q=\frac{1}{x^{2}}$ 

Now, IF $=e^{\int (-2/x)dx}=e^{-2\log x}=1/x^{2}$

Solution is $y\left (\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right )=\int \left (\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right )\frac{1}{x^{2}}dx$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & \Rightarrow \frac{y}{x^{2}}=\int \frac{1}{x^{4}}dx\Rightarrow \frac{y}{x^{2}}=-\frac{1}{3x^{3}}+C \\  \\  & \Rightarrow y=-\frac{1}{3x}+Cx^{2} \end{array}$

Given, $f(1)=\frac{2}{3}$.

So, $\frac{2}{3}=-\frac{1}{3}+C\Rightarrow C=1$

Thus, $y=f(x)=-\frac{1}{3x}+x^{2}$

$\therefore 18f(3)=18\left \{9-\frac{1}{9}\right \}=18\times \frac{80}{9}=160$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: Let the first term $α$ and the common ratio r of a geometric progression be positive integers. If the sum of squares of its first three terms is 33033, then the sum of these three terms is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that the first term $a$ and common ratio $r$ of a geometric progression be positive integers. So, their 1st three terms are $a,ar,ar^{2}$

According to the question, $a^{2}+a^{2}r^{2}+a^{2}r^{4}=33033$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow a^{2}\left (1+r^{2}+r^{4}\right ) & =3\times 7\times 11\times 11\times 13 \\ =3\times 7\times 13\times 11^{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \quad a^{2}=11^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow a=11 \\  \\ \text{and}1+r^{2}+r^{4}=273 \\  \\ \Rightarrow r^{2}+r^{4}=272 \\  \\ \Rightarrow r^{4}+r^{2}-272=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \left (r^{2}+17\right )\left (r^{2}-16\right )=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow r^{2}=-17(notpossible), \\  \\ \Rightarrow r^{2}-16=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow r=\pm 4 \\  \\ \Rightarrow r=4(\because r>0) \end{array}$

So, sum of these first three terms is $a+ar+ar^{2}$ $=11+44+176=231$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift

text: Let the complex number $z=x+iy$ be such that $\frac{2z-3i}{2z+i}$ is purely imaginary. If $x+y^{2}=0$, then $y^{4}+y^{2}-y$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $z=x+iy$

So, $\frac{2z-3i}{2z+i}$ is purely imaginary
[MATH$_$FAILED][Given]

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Now,}\left (\dfrac{2z-3i}{2z+i}\right )+\left (\dfrac{2z-3i–}{2z+i}\right )=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{2z-3i}{2z+i}+\dfrac{2\bar{z}+3i}{2\bar{z}-i}=0 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow (2z-3i)(2\bar{z}-i)+(2\bar{z}+3i)(2z+i)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \left \{4|z|^{2}-6i\bar{z}-2iz-3\right \}+\left \{4|z|^{2}+6iz+2i\bar{z}-3\right \}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 8|z|^{2}-4i\bar{z}+4iz-6=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 8\left (x^{2}+y^{2}\right )-4i(x-iy)+4i(x+iy)-6=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 8\left (x^{2}+y^{2}\right )-4ix-4y+4ix-4y-6=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 8\left (x^{2}+y^{2}\right )-8y-6=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 4\left (x^{2}+y^{2}\right )-4y-3=0 \end{array}$

Given that, $x+y^{2}=0$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow x=-y^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 4\left (y^{4}+y^{2}\right )-4y=3 \\  \\ \Rightarrow y^{4}+y^{2}-y=\dfrac{3}{4} \end{array}$

Hence, required answer is $\frac{3}{4}$.

text: Let $f:(-2,2)\to R$ be defined by $f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x[x], & -2<x<0 \\ (x-1)[x], & 0\leq x<2 \end{array} \right.$ where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer function. If m and n respectively are the number of points in $(-2,2)$ at which $y=|f(x)|$ is not continuous and not differentiable, then $m+n$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given function is $f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x[x], & -2<x<0 \\ (x-1)[x], & 0\leq x<2 \end{array} \right.$ 

where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer function


[IMG]


Clearly, $|f(x)|$ remains same.

Given that, $m$ and $n$ respectively are the number of points in $(-2,2)$ at which $y=|f(x)|$ is not continuous and not differentiable

So, $m=1$ where $y=|f(x)|$ not continuous

and $n=3$ where $|f(x)|$ is not differentiable.

Thus, $m+n=4$

text: Let $y=p(x)$ be the parabola passing through the points $(-1,0),(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$. If the area of the region $\{(x,y):(x+1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}\leq 1,y\leq p(x)\}$ is A, then $12(π-4A)$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $y=p(x)$ be the parabola passing through the points $(-1,0)(0,1)(1,0)$.

Now, to find the area of the region

$\left \{(x,y);(x+1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}\leq 1,y\leq p(x)\right \}$


[IMG]


Thus, area of shaded region is

$\begin{array}{l} A=\int\limits _{-1}^{0}\left \{\left (1-x^{2}\right )-\left (1-\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}\right \}dx \\  \\ =\int\limits _{-1}^{0}\left \{-x^{2}+\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}\right \}dx \\  \\ =\int\limits _{-1}^{0}-x^{2}dx+\int\limits _{-1}^{0}\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}dx \\  \\ =-\left (\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right )_{-1}^{0}+\left [\dfrac{\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}\sin ^{-1}(x+1)\right ]_{-1}^{0} \\  \\ =-\dfrac{1}{3}+\left [\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{π}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}\right ] \\  \\ A=\dfrac{π}{4}-\dfrac{1}{3} \end{array} \right.$

Now, $12(π-4A)$

$\begin{array}{l} =12\left [π-4\left (\dfrac{π}{4}-\dfrac{1}{3}\right )\right ] \\  \\ =12\left (π-π+\dfrac{4}{3}\right )=16 \end{array}$

text: The number of elements in the set $\{n\in Z:|n^{2}-10n+19|<6\}$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\left |n^{2}-10n+19\right |<6$ 

$\Rightarrow -6<n^{2}-10n+19<6$

Take, $-6<n^{2}-10n+19$ and $n^{2}-10n+19<6$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow n^{2}-10n+25>0 & \text{and}n^{2}-10n+13<0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow (n-5)^{2}>0 & \text{and}5-2\sqrt{3}<n<5+2\sqrt{3} \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow n\in \mathrm{ℤ}-\{5\}$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & \therefore n\in (5-2\sqrt{3},5+2\sqrt{3}) \\  \\  & \therefore n\in (1.54,8.46) \\  \\  & \therefore n=2,3,4,6,7,8 \end{array}$

Thus, number of elements in the set is 6

is 28, then its variance is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given mean is 28

$\begin{array}{l} \text{So,}\frac{2\times 5+3\times 15+x\times 25+5\times 35+4\times 45}{14+x}=28 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \frac{10+45+25x+175+180}{14+x}=28 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 410+25x=392+28x \\  \\ \Rightarrow 3x=18\Rightarrow x=6 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \text{Variance}=\left (\dfrac{\sum x_{i}^{2}f_{i}}{\sum f_{i}}\right )-(\text{mean})^{2} \\  \\ =\left (\dfrac{2\times 5^{2}+3\times 15^{2}+6\times 25^{2}+5\times 35^{2}+4\times 45^{2}}{20}\right )-(28)^{2} \\  \\ =\left (\dfrac{50+675+3750+6125+8100}{20}\right )-(28)^{2} \\  \\ =\left (\dfrac{18700}{20}\right )-(28)^{2} \\  \\ =935-784=151 \end{array}$

text: The number of permutations, of the digits 1, 2, 3, ..., 7 without repetition, which neither contain the string 153 nor the string 2467, is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that digits are $1,2,3,4,5,6,7$

Total permutations $=7$!

Let $p=$ Number which containing string 153

$q=$ Number which containing string 2467

$\begin{array}{ll}  & \therefore n(p)=5!\times 1 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow n(q)=4!\times 1 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow n(p\cap q)=2! \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore n(p\cup q)=n(p)+n(q)-n(p\cap q) \\  \\ =5!+4!-2!=120+24-2=142 \end{array}$

$\therefore n$ (neither string 143 nor string 2467)

$=7!-142=5040-142=4898$

text: Some couples participated in a mixed doubles badminton tournament. If the number of matches played, so that no couple played in a match, is 840, then the total number of persons, who participated in the tournament, is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $n$ be the total number of couples who participated in the tournament.

According to the question, $2\times {}^{n}C_{2}\times {}^{n-2}C_{2}=840$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow {}^{n}C_{2}\times {}^{n-2}C_{2}=420 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{n!}{2!(n-2)!}\times \dfrac{(n-2)!}{(n-4)!2!}=420 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}{4}=420 \end{array}$

$n=8$ satisfies the equation.

So, $n=8$

Hence, total number of players who participated
in the tournament $=2\times 8=16$

text:
Let a, b, c be three distinct positive real numbers such that $(2a)^{\log _{e}a}=(bc)^{\log _{e}b}$ and $b^{\log _{e}2}=a^{\log _{e}c}$.

Then, 6a + 5bc is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 10th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $(2a)^{\ln a}=(bc)^{\ln b}$, where $2a>0,bc>0$

$\Rightarrow \ln a(\ln 2+\ln a)=\ln b(\ln b+\ln c)$ ..........(i)

and
$(b)^{\ln 2}=(a)^{\ln c}$

$\Rightarrow \ln 2\cdot \ln b=\ln c\cdot \ln a$ ..........(ii)

Now, let $\ln a=x,\ln b=y$

$\ln 2=p,\ln c=z$

Now, from Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$p\cdot y=xz\text{and}x(p+x)=y(y+z)$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore p=\dfrac{xz}{y} \\  \\ \therefore x\left (\dfrac{xz}{y}+x\right )=y(y+z) \\  \\ \Rightarrow x^{2}z+x^{2}y=y^{2}(y+z) \\  \\ \Rightarrow \left (x^{2}-y^{2}\right )(y+z)=0 \end{array}$
$\therefore$ $x^{2}=y^{2}$

$x=\pm y$

So, from the equations, there are two cases :

Case 1 :

$x=y$

In this case, since x and y are natural logarithms of positive numbers a and b respectively, this implies that a = b. However, this cannot be true as a, b, and c are given to be distinct positive real numbers.

Case 2 :

x = -y

In this case, $\ln a=-\ln b$

$\Rightarrow a\times b=1$

$\Rightarrow b=\frac{1}{a}$

Also, y + z = 0 (from the equations above)

$\Rightarrow \ln b+\ln c=0$

$\Rightarrow \ln (b\times c)=0$

$\Rightarrow b\times c=1$

Given $b=\frac{1}{a}$ and $b\times c=1$
$\Rightarrow c=a$

Thus, in the case where x = -y, the possible values are :
 

$b=\frac{1}{a}$
 

$c=a$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{If}bc=1\Rightarrow (2a)^{\ln a}=1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow a=1/2 \\  \\ \text{So,}6a+5bc=6\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )+5=3+5=8 \end{array}$
